#### 1. Schwartz-Jampel syndrome type 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.434)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1474228, Reactome:R-HSA-216083)

**Proposed mechanism:** FBN1 (HGNC:3003) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); HSPG2 (HGNC:4921) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0000007); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004325); FBN1 (HGNC:3003) —LEADS_TO→ Myopia (HP:0000540); HSPG2 (HGNC:4921) —LEADS_TO→ Joint stiffness (HP:0001366). Mutations in FBN1 (causing Stiff skin syndrome) and HSPG2 (causing Schwartz-Jampel syndrome type 1) both disrupt the crucial process of extracellular matrix organization. This shared disruption leads to overlapping phenotypes such as skeletal abnormalities and short stature, and also contributes to specific phenotypes like myopia (associated with FBN1) and joint stiffness (associated with HSPG2).

**How to falsify it:** The hypothesis would be falsified if genetic analysis revealed that the causal variants for Stiff skin syndrome (in FBN1) and Schwartz-Jampel syndrome type 1 (in HSPG2) do not converge on the extracellular matrix organization pathway, or if distinct molecular mechanisms unrelated to matrix integrity could fully explain the phenotypes of both diseases.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of extracellular matrix disruption in both Stiff skin syndrome and Schwartz-Jampel syndrome type 1 could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring extracellular matrix integrity or function, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
